# `unused-local`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: semantic · Profile: none · Default: error · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a local constant or variable, function parameter, or capture that
nothing references, which AstGen rejects.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Zig rejects a local binding that nothing uses: AstGen reports "unused local
constant", "unused local variable", "unused function parameter", "unused
capture" or "unused switch tag capture", and the file does not compile. The
binding is usually left over from a refactor, or a sign that the value was
meant to be used and the code that should read it is missing. Reporting it
from the analyzer shows the error while editing, before any build, and in
files the compiler has not reached yet.

## When it fires

It reports a `const` or `var` declared in a block (a function, test or
`comptime` body, at any depth), a parameter of a function with a body, and a
payload, index or error capture of `if`, `while`, `for`, `switch` and `catch`
when no identifier spelled like it (quoted `@"name"` forms included) follows
it in its scope other than as a field or member name. Declarations directly
in a container, parameters of `extern` functions and function types, and
names spelled `_` are not checked, as the compiler does not check them. A
file with syntax errors is skipped.

The message and span are the compiler's own, so an editor that also shows
compile errors displays one diagnostic. The quick fix discards the binding:
`_ = name;` after a constant or at the start of the body for a parameter,
`_ = &name;` for a variable (which also keeps it from being reported as never
mutated), `|_|` for a payload capture, and removing the capture where a
discard is not allowed (`catch |err|`, `else |err|`, a lone switch payload, a
switch tag). The index capture of an unbounded range cannot be discarded, so
it has no fix.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
pub fn main() void {
    const answer = 42;
}
```
